verdict: The byte-capture change preserves child status, watchdog rejection, input/binary drift rejection and completed-record hashing. One transitive dependency hash omission is reported separately; no product input or active root validation log was touched.

scope: Static read-only comparison against original run.py plus isolated record() probes. The current snapshot includes additional collector binding/invocation and corrected non-atomic write wording, so it is not described as a single-hunk-only change.
capture_findings: subprocess.run receives identical argv/cwd/environment/timeout; stdout=PIPE and stderr=STDOUT replace streaming to an open text file. Successful child output is captured as bytes, then written once after subprocess completion.

A completed command JSON and matching hashes establish acceptance; open/write is not an atomic rename and a concurrent reader could observe an incomplete physical write before command metadata exists.
Nonzero child exit is preserved. Timeout becomes exit124 with captured TimeoutExpired.stdout and an explicit watchdog marker, and remains a failure.
Preexisting log paths prevent launching the child; exclusive binary write still refuses replacement. Command metadata remains exclusive-create.
Source inputs are checked before and after; a successful child cannot override source drift or non-build artifact drift.

Full-stage result collection is now invoked with check=True; collector verifies complete CTest counts, successful commands, manifest/log hashes and fifteen unique native markers with matching pass summaries.
